w: Nice's Russian Orthodox cemetery sits in the Caucade district, southwest of the centre - rows of Orthodox crosses and modest headstones, one of the city's quieter, least-visited corners, tucked well away from the Promenade des Anglais crowds.
s: Orthodox crosses in Nice's quiet Caucade quarter
_facts: Russian Orthodox cemetery, also known as the Orthodox cemetery in Caucade

w: A national art school and a national contemporary art centre share one hillside address, chartered by the Ministry of Culture in 1972. The Centre National d'Art Contemporain half is open to the public - free contemporary shows in a building built to train the artists making the next ones.
s: A national contemporary art centre on the hill
_facts: Art museum, art school and research institution for contemporary art in Nice, created by ministerial charter in 1972
Houses both the Ecole Nationale Superieure d'Arts de Nice and the Centre National d'Art Contemporain

n: Jardin Botanique de la Ville de Nice
w: A free, city-run botanical garden on the Corniche Fleurie, 3.5 hectares open every day of the year without charge - a low-key alternative to Nice's grander, more manicured green spaces, and easy to have almost to yourself.
s: Free botanical garden, open daily, no charge
_facts: 3.5-hectare municipal botanical garden at 78 avenue de la Corniche Fleurie, Nice

w: Built in the 1780s and later given away by Cecile Furtado-Heine, a Jewish philanthropist, to house army officers convalescing after France's expedition to Madagascar - an odd colonial footnote preserved as a national monument since 1961.
s: A philanthropist's mansion for wounded soldiers
_facts: Donated by philanthropist Cecile Furtado-Heine for the convalescence of army officers returning from the French expedition to Madagascar; listed national monument since 10 June 1961

w: An 18th-century mansion, built in the 1760s and quietly listed as a national monument since 1949 - one of Nice's older private houses to survive intact, with barely a public record beyond its own facade.
_facts: Listed as an official national monument since 16 December 1949

w: Built between 1884 and 1887 for Victoire Schmitz and designed by architect Vincent Levrot, this villa only gained its national monument listing in 2010 - one more of Nice's private Belle Epoque houses only recently recognised.
s: A Belle Epoque villa, listed only since 2010
_facts: Historic mansion in Nice, built 1884-1887 for Victoire Schmitz, designed by architect Vincent Levrot
Listed as an official national monument since 1 October 2010
